tests.title: The rebuild creates a detached worktree at the deterministic per-job path with HEAD at the resolved upstream base
given: a workspace "acme" with trunk at <root>/acme/trunk
the context carries job id "job-42"
the upstream base has resolved to SHA U
then: the trunk's GitRunner receives WorktreeAdd("<root>/acme/rebuild/job-42", detached=true, U)
a directory exists at that path afterward
rev-parse HEAD run against the worktree's runner returns U
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctxWithJobID("job-42"), payload); assert trunkRunner.WorktreeAddCalls[0] == {path: "acme/rebuild/job-42", detach:true, commitish:U}; assert dirExists("acme/rebuild/job-42")

tests.title: A context with no job ID falls back to a generated UUID for the worktree path and logs a warning
given: a context that does not carry a job id (jobqueue.JobIDFromContext returns "")
then: the worktree path's last segment is a valid UUID, not empty
a warn-level log line records the substitution
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(context.Background(), payload); path := trunkRunner.WorktreeAddCalls[0].path; assert isUUID(basename(path)); assert logger.WarnCalls contains substring("job id")

tests.title: Cherry-pick, merge, rerere, rev-parse, conflict-diff and abort/reset commands run against the worktree's GitRunner, not the trunk's
given: a rebuild with one active patch that applies cleanly and one that conflicts
then: CherryPick, MergeNoFF, rerere, rev-parse, `diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`, and the conflict abort/reset calls are all recorded on worktreeRunner
none of those calls appear on trunkRunner
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert worktreeRunner.CherryPickCalls non-empty; assert worktreeRunner.RunCalls contains "rerere"; assert trunkRunner.RunCalls does not contain "cherry-pick" or "rerere"

tests.title: The trunk's runner never receives checkout, reset, cherry-pick, merge, rebase, gc --prune=now or reflog expire, other than the one-time _rebuild_temp deletion
given: a rebuild that hits a conflict, aborts, and a separate run where _rebuild_temp pre-exists
tests.when: the rebuild executes end to end in each scenario
then: trunkRunner.RunCalls contains no "checkout", "reset", "cherry-pick", "merge", "rebase", "gc" with "--prune=now", or "reflog" with "expire" arguments
the only trunk-mutating call besides ref reads is "branch -D _rebuild_temp" when that branch exists
tests.pseudocode: for scenario in [conflict, rebuildTempPresent]: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert none(trunkRunner.RunCalls, forbiddenVerbs)

tests.title: A successful rebuild force-updates the integration branch from the worktree's final HEAD SHA without checking it out
given: the trunk is currently checked out onto "main"
patch application in the worktree finishes at SHA F
then: trunkRunner receives exactly "branch -f deploy F"
trunkRunner never receives a "checkout" of "deploy"
currentCheckout(trunk) is still "main" afterward
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert trunkRunner.RunCalls contains ["branch","-f","deploy",F]; assert currentCheckout(trunkRunner)=="main"

tests.title: rerere.enabled and rerere.autoupdate are configured on a runner backed by the shared .git config
given: a fresh rebuild run
tests.when: the executor configures rerere before applying patches
then: a "git config rerere.enabled true" and a "git config rerere.autoupdate true" call are recorded on either the trunk or the worktree runner
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); calls := trunkRunner.RunCalls + worktreeRunner.RunCalls; assert calls contains ["config","rerere.enabled","true"]; assert calls contains ["config","rerere.autoupdate","true"]

tests.title: The trunk's HEAD, index and working tree are byte-for-byte identical before and after any rebuild outcome
given: a real trunk clone with a captured pre-run snapshot (HEAD sha, index digest, working-tree file hashes)
tests.when: for any rebuild outcome in {success, unresolved-conflict-fail-fast, unresolved-conflict-continue, transient-error, cancellation}, the rebuild runs to completion
then: the post-run HEAD sha, index digest and working-tree file hashes equal the pre-run snapshot in every case
tests.pseudocode: for outcome in outcomes: before := snapshot(trunkDir); h.HandleRebuildJob(ctxFor(outcome), payload); after := snapshot(trunkDir); assert before == after

tests.title: Every exit path removes the worktree with --force and then prunes, from the trunk's runner
given: four scenarios: success, unresolved conflict under fail_fast, unresolved conflict under continue mode ending the run, transient error, and a cancelled context
tests.when: each scenario runs to its exit
then: trunkRunner receives WorktreeRemove(path, force=true) followed by WorktreePrune() in every scenario
tests.pseudocode: for scenario in scenarios: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctxFor(scenario), payload); assert trunkRunner.WorktreeRemoveCalls[-1]=={path, force:true}; assert trunkRunner.WorktreePruneCalls non-empty

tests.title: A failed worktree removal or prune is logged but does not change the job's recorded outcome
given: trunkRunner.WorktreeRemove and WorktreePrune are stubbed to return errors
a rebuild that would otherwise succeed
then: the returned result, retryable flag and error are identical to the same run with removal succeeding
a log line records the removal failure
tests.pseudocode: resultA,_,errA := h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload) // removal fails; resultB,_,errB := h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload) // removal succeeds; assert resultA==resultB && errA==errB

tests.title: Before creating its worktree, the rebuild removes every existing directory under <slug>/rebuild/ and prunes
given: <root>/acme/rebuild/ already contains stale directories "old-job-1" and "old-job-2"
tests.when: a new rebuild job for "acme" starts
then: "old-job-1" and "old-job-2" no longer exist once the new worktree is created
trunkRunner.WorktreePruneCalls includes a call preceding the WorktreeAdd call
tests.pseudocode: makeDirs("acme/rebuild/old-job-1","acme/rebuild/old-job-2"); h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert !dirExists("acme/rebuild/old-job-1"); assert !dirExists("acme/rebuild/old-job-2")

tests.title: Hub startup removes every workspace's rebuild directory and prunes its trunk before job dispatch begins
given: two workspaces "acme" and "beta" each with a stale <slug>/rebuild/<job-id> directory
tests.when: the startup cleanup routine runs, prior to mergeQueue.Start()
then: neither stale directory exists afterward
each trunk's runner recorded a WorktreePrune call
the job queue had not yet dispatched any job when the cleanup ran
tests.pseudocode: startupCleanup(workspaceRoot, workspaces); assert !dirExists("acme/rebuild"); assert !dirExists("beta/rebuild"); assert dispatchStartedAfter(cleanupTimestamp)

tests.title: A rebuild started after a simulated crash begins cleanly with no trunk reset
given: a prior rebuild left <slug>/rebuild/job-7 on disk with an in-progress cherry-pick state and no guard/lock held (simulating a crash)
tests.when: a fresh rebuild job for the same workspace is dispatched
then: the stale directory is removed before the new worktree is created
the trunk's runner never receives checkout, reset or cherry-pick calls
the rebuild completes successfully
tests.pseudocode: seedStaleWorktree("acme","job-7"); result,_,err := h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert err==nil; assert !dirExists("acme/rebuild/job-7"); assert trunkRunner.RunCalls has no "reset" or "cherry-pick"

tests.title: After resolving the upstream base under the fetch-phase lock, the executor checks for a local _rebuild_temp branch
given: the fetch-phase lock has just been acquired and resolveUpstreamBase has returned
then: trunkRunner receives "rev-parse --verify refs/heads/_rebuild_temp" before the fetch-phase lock is released
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); idx := indexOf(trunkRunner.RunCalls, ["rev-parse","--verify","refs/heads/_rebuild_temp"]); assert idx >= 0 && idx < indexOfUnlock

tests.title: When _rebuild_temp is the currently checked-out branch, the trunk is checked out onto the configured branch, or left detached, before deletion
given: scenario A: _rebuild_temp exists, is currently checked out, and the workspace branch is "main"
scenario B: same but the workspace has no configured branch
then: in scenario A, trunkRunner receives "checkout main" before "branch -D _rebuild_temp"
in scenario B, trunkRunner receives "checkout --detach" at _rebuild_temp's tip before "branch -D _rebuild_temp"
tests.pseudocode: for scenario in [A,B]: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert order(trunkRunner.RunCalls, expectedCheckout(scenario), ["branch","-D","_rebuild_temp"])

tests.title: An existing _rebuild_temp branch is deleted with branch -D and the deletion is logged at info with the workspace slug
given: _rebuild_temp exists in the trunk but is not currently checked out
then: trunkRunner receives "branch -D _rebuild_temp"
an info-level log line names workspace slug "acme" and mentions _rebuild_temp
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert trunkRunner.RunCalls contains ["branch","-D","_rebuild_temp"]; assert logger.InfoCalls contains substring("acme") && substring("_rebuild_temp")

tests.title: When no _rebuild_temp branch exists, the executor skips checkout and deletion and leaves the trunk's HEAD and branch unchanged
given: no local branch named _rebuild_temp exists in the trunk
the trunk is checked out onto "main" at SHA M
then: trunkRunner never receives a "checkout" or "branch -D _rebuild_temp" call
currentCheckout(trunk) is still "main" at SHA M after the fetch phase
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert trunkRunner.RunCalls has no "checkout" call and no ["branch","-D","_rebuild_temp"]; assert currentCheckout(trunkRunner)==("main",M)

tests.title: The rebuild-active guard is set before the fetch-phase TryLock is attempted
given: a fresh rebuild job for "acme"
then: the guard-set call for "acme" is recorded strictly before the wslock.TryLock("acme") call
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert order(callLog, ["guard.Set","acme"], ["wslock.TryLock","acme"])

tests.title: A failed fetch-phase TryLock returns a retryable TransientError without doing any fetch-phase work
given: wslock.TryLock("acme") is stubbed to fail because another operation holds the lock
then: the returned error is a *TransientError
the retryable flag is true
no Fetch call, resolveUpstreamBase call, or _rebuild_temp rev-parse call was made
tests.pseudocode: _, retryable, err := h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert retryable==true; assert errors.As(err,&TransientError{}); assert fetchCalls==0 && trunkRunner.RunCalls has no "_rebuild_temp" rev-parse

tests.title: Once the fetch-phase lock is acquired, fetch, upstream-base resolution and _rebuild_temp cleanup run, then the lock is released before the worktree is created
given: wslock.TryLock("acme") succeeds
then: Fetch, resolveUpstreamBase and the _rebuild_temp check all complete before the unlock call
the unlock call happens before WorktreeAdd is called
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert order(callLog, fetchCall, resolveBaseCall, rebuildTempCheck, unlockCall, worktreeAddCall)

tests.title: Archive and reclone answer 409 workspace_busy while the rebuild-active guard is set, and leave the workspace directory untouched
given: a rebuild for "acme" has set the rebuild-active guard and is applying patches
tests.when: POST /workspaces/acme/archive and POST /workspaces/acme/reclone are each called
then: both respond 409 with error type workspace_busy
the workspace directory <root>/acme still exists with its trunk intact
tests.pseudocode: recArchive := doRequest(POST,'/workspaces/acme/archive'); recReclone := doRequest(POST,'/workspaces/acme/reclone'); assert recArchive.Code==409 && recArchive.json.error_type=="workspace_busy"; assert recReclone.Code==409; assert dirExists("acme/trunk")

tests.title: The rebuild-active guard is cleared unconditionally, via defer, once the worktree has been removed on any exit path
given: scenarios: success, conflict, transient error, cancellation
then: the guard for "acme" is unset after the run in every scenario
the guard-clear call happens after the WorktreeRemove call in each scenario
tests.pseudocode: for scenario in scenarios: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctxFor(scenario), payload); assert guard.IsSet("acme")==false; assert order(callLog,["WorktreeRemove"],["guard.Clear","acme"])

tests.title: No rebuild worktree is created while archive or reclone holds the workspace lock
given: archive is mid-run and holds wslock.Lock("acme") (not yet released)
tests.when: a rebuild job for "acme" is dispatched
then: the fetch-phase TryLock fails
the rebuild returns a retryable error
no <root>/acme/rebuild/* directory is created
tests.pseudocode: unlock := wslock.Lock("acme"); _, retryable, err := h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert retryable==true; assert !dirExists("acme/rebuild"); unlock()

tests.title: Sync, rollback, rerere forget, batch rebase and merge jobs proceed for a workspace whose rebuild is applying patches
given: a rebuild for "acme" has released the fetch-phase lock and is applying patches, before the final-phase lock is taken
tests.when: POST /sync, a rollback request, a rerere-forget request, a batch-rebase request and a merge job for "acme" are each attempted
then: none of them respond 409 workspace_busy or are blocked by the merge job's queue
tests.pseudocode: assert doRequest(POST,'/workspaces/acme/sync').Code != 409; assert doRequest(POST,'/rollback').Code != 409; assert doRequest(DELETE,'/rerere/x').Code != 409

tests.title: The git server's post-push handler resets the trunk's working tree normally while a rebuild is applying patches
given: a rebuild for "acme" is between its fetch and final phases, applying patches
a client pushes a new commit to the trunk via the hub's git server
then: wslock.TryLock("acme") succeeds for the post-push handler
the trunk's working tree is reset to the newly pushed commit
no "workspace busy; skipping worktree reset" log line is produced
tests.pseudocode: push("acme", newCommit); assert trunkWorkingTreeHEAD()==newCommit; assert logger.WarnCalls does not contain "skipping worktree reset"

tests.title: A concurrent sync that advances upstream does not change the upstream base an in-flight rebuild is using
given: a rebuild resolved upstream base U during its fetch phase and released the lock
tests.when: POST /sync fetches upstream and updates upstream_head_sha to a newer commit V while patches are still being applied
then: the rebuild's remaining cherry-pick/merge calls still target commits derived from U, never V
tests.pseudocode: captured := rebuildState.upstreamBase; triggerConcurrentSync(newUpstream=V); assert rebuildState.upstreamBase==captured && captured!=V

tests.title: Sync's auto-rebuild enqueue is deduplicated against an already-active rebuild job for the same (type, key)
given: a rebuild job for "acme" is already queued/running with key "acme:deploy"
tests.when: POST /sync triggers its own auto-rebuild enqueue for the same key
then: no second row is inserted into the jobs table for (type=rebuild, key=acme:deploy)
tests.pseudocode: before := countJobs("rebuild","acme:deploy"); doRequest(POST,'/workspaces/acme/sync'); after := countJobs("rebuild","acme:deploy"); assert after==before

tests.title: Objects reachable only from a worktree's HEAD survive a git gc run by another operation against the trunk
given: a real git repository with a worktree whose HEAD points at a commit not reachable from any trunk ref
tests.when: for any such dangling-from-trunk commit made reachable solely via a worktree's HEAD, `git gc --prune=now` is run in the trunk
then: the commit and its tree/blobs are still present and readable after gc
tests.pseudocode: for commit in gen_commits(): addWorktreeAtDetached(commit); run(trunk, "gc","--prune=now"); assert objectExists(trunk, commit)

tests.title: The blocking workspace lock is reacquired before the integration-branch ref update, on both success and a fail_fast abort after cleanup
given: scenario A: patch application succeeds
scenario B: patch application hits an unresolved conflict under fail_fast
tests.when: each scenario reaches its post-patch-application step
then: wslock.Lock("acme") is called before any "branch -f"/ref-update call in scenario A
in scenario B, the lock is still (re)acquired for the equivalent bookkeeping before the run exits
tests.pseudocode: for scenario in [A,B]: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctxFor(scenario), payload); assert order(callLog, ["wslock.Lock","acme"], refUpdateOrEquivalent(scenario))

tests.title: While the final-phase lock is held, only the ref update, stale-patch comparison, soft-deletion, compaction and optional push run
given: a successful rebuild with one merged_upstream patch and REBUILD_PUSH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH=true
then: the operations performed between Lock and Unlock are exactly: branch -f, SoftDeletePatch, CompactPositions, and PushIntegration
no patch application command appears in that window
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); ops := callLog.between("wslock.Lock","wslock.Unlock"); assert set(ops) subsetOf {"branch-f","SoftDeletePatch","CompactPositions","PushIntegration","revParseVerify"}

tests.title: The final-phase lock is released before the worktree is removed
given: a successful rebuild run
then: the wslock.Unlock call for "acme" happens before the WorktreeRemove call
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert order(callLog, ["wslock.Unlock","acme"], ["WorktreeRemove"])

tests.title: The rebuild's integration-branch update wins over an interleaved rollback
given: a rollback for "acme" acquires wslock while the rebuild is still applying patches and force-updates the integration branch to an older SHA, then releases the lock
tests.when: the rebuild's final phase subsequently reacquires the lock and runs its own branch -f to its final HEAD SHA F
then: once both operations have completed, the integration branch points at F, not the rollback's SHA
tests.pseudocode: runRollbackConcurrently("acme"); h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert revParse(trunk,"deploy")==F

tests.title: The final phase always uses the blocking Lock, never TryLock, even when the lock is already held by another operation
given: wslock is held by a merge job for "acme" when the rebuild's patch application finishes
tests.when: the rebuild reaches its final phase
then: the rebuild calls wslock.Lock (blocking), not wslock.TryLock
the rebuild's final phase proceeds only after the merge job releases the lock, without returning an error for lock contention
tests.pseudocode: unlock := wslock.Lock("acme"); go func(){ time.Sleep(d); unlock() }(); _, _, err := h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert err==nil; assert calledBlockingLockNotTryLock

tests.title: Patch branches are resolved to SHAs before applying the first patch, and those SHAs, not branch names, drive commit selection and application
given: two active patches on branches "feature/a" and "feature/b" at SHAs A and B
then: rev-parse --verify refs/heads/feature/a and .../feature/b both run before any cherry-pick/merge call
the subsequent git log / CherryPick / MergeNoFF calls reference A and B, not the branch names
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert order(callLog, snapshotCalls, firstApplyCall); assert applyCalls reference {A,B} not {"feature/a","feature/b"}

tests.title: A merge-strategy commit message names the source branch, not its snapshot SHA
given: strategy is merge, patch branch "feature/a" snapshotted at SHA A
tests.when: the merge --no-ff for that patch runs
then: the resulting commit message contains "feature/a"
the commit message does not contain the raw SHA A
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); msg := worktreeRunner.lastMergeCommitMessage; assert contains(msg,"feature/a") && !contains(msg,A)

tests.title: A patch branch that fails to resolve at snapshot time is recorded as skipped/branch_not_found and the run continues
given: a patch record whose branch_name does not exist as a ref
another active patch that resolves fine
then: that patch's PatchResult has status "skipped" and skipped_reason "branch_not_found"
the other patch is still processed and appears with its own result
tests.pseudocode: result,_,_ := h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); pr := findResult(result.PatchResults, missingPatchID); assert pr.Status=="skipped" && pr.SkippedReason=="branch_not_found"; assert len(result.PatchResults)==2

tests.title: After the final-phase lock is released, active-at-snapshot patch tips are re-read against the trunk's runner without holding a lock
given: two patches were 'active' at snapshot time
the final phase has just released wslock
then: rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<branch> is called for each of those two patches after the unlock call and while no lock is held
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert order(callLog, ["wslock.Unlock"], compareCalls); assert lockHeldDuring(compareCalls)==false

tests.title: A moved active-patch tip enqueues a follow-up rebuild job with the expected payload shape when AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH is not "false"
given: patch "feature/a" was snapshotted at SHA A but now resolves to SHA A2
AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH is unset (default, not "false")
the current job's Group/Key are "acme"/"acme:deploy"
tests.when: the stale-tip comparison finds the moved tip
then: a new job row exists with type rebuild, SubmittedBy "system:stale-snapshot", the same Group/Key "acme:deploy", and a nonce different from the current job's
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); job := findLatestJob("rebuild","acme:deploy"); assert job.SubmittedBy=="system:stale-snapshot"; assert job.Nonce != currentJob.Nonce

tests.title: Skipped, disabled, conflicted, merged and deleted patches are excluded from the stale-tip comparison
given: one active patch unchanged
one disabled patch whose branch was pushed to during the run
one merged_upstream patch also pushed to
then: no follow-up job is enqueued as a result of the disabled or merged_upstream patches' movement
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert countJobs("rebuild", groupKey) == before

tests.title: Each patch result records its snapshot SHA as source_sha alongside new_head_sha
given: a patch snapshotted at SHA A that applies successfully to new HEAD SHA F
then: that patch's PatchResult has source_sha == A and new_head_sha == F
tests.pseudocode: result,_,_ := h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); pr := findResult(result.PatchResults, patchID); assert pr.SourceSHA==A && *pr.NewHeadSHA==F

tests.title: Enqueuing a follow-up rebuild emits a hub.rebuild.followup audit event listing the stale patch branch names
given: patches "feature/a" and "feature/c" both moved past their snapshot SHAs
AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH is not "false"
then: a hub.rebuild.followup audit event is emitted whose metadata lists ["feature/a","feature/c"]
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); ev := findAuditEvent("hub.rebuild.followup"); assert set(ev.Metadata["stale_branches"]) == {"feature/a","feature/c"}

tests.title: Cancellation during patch application aborts the in-progress operation in the worktree, removes it, clears the guard, and returns the trunk-era retryable error shape scoped to the worktree
given: a rebuild is mid cherry-pick in its worktree
the job context is cancelled
then: worktreeRunner receives a "cherry-pick --abort" (or "merge --abort") call
the worktree directory no longer exists afterward
the rebuild-active guard for the workspace is cleared
the returned error is retryable and of the same type the trunk-based cancellation path returned
tests.pseudocode: ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background()); cancel(); _, retryable, err := h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert retryable==true; assert !dirExists(worktreePath); assert guard.IsSet("acme")==false; assert sameErrorShape(err, legacyCancellationError)

tests.title: A failed abort during cancellation still results in the worktree being removed and the guard being cleared
given: cancellation occurs mid cherry-pick
worktreeRunner's abort call is stubbed to fail
then: a log line records the abort failure
the worktree directory no longer exists
the rebuild-active guard is cleared
tests.pseudocode: _, _, err := h.HandleRebuildJob(cancelledCtx, payload); assert logger.WarnCalls contains substring("abort"); assert !dirExists(worktreePath); assert guard.IsSet("acme")==false

tests.title: Cancellation during the fetch phase, before the worktree exists, releases the lock, clears the guard and returns a retryable error without creating a worktree
given: a rebuild job's context is cancelled while wslock.TryLock is held during the fetch phase, before WorktreeAdd is called
then: wslock is released for the workspace
the rebuild-active guard is cleared
the returned error is retryable
no worktree directory was ever created
tests.pseudocode: _, retryable, err := h.HandleRebuildJob(cancelledDuringFetchCtx, payload); assert retryable==true; assert !wslock.IsLocked("acme"); assert guard.IsSet("acme")==false; assert trunkRunner.WorktreeAddCalls==empty

tests.title: hub.rebuild.complete and hub.rebuild.fail keep the same fields as before this change
given: one scenario that succeeds and one that errors transiently
then: a hub.rebuild.complete event with a patches_applied field is emitted on success
a hub.rebuild.fail event with a reason field is emitted on the error path
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, successPayload); assert findAuditEvent("hub.rebuild.complete").Metadata["patches_applied"] != nil; h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, failingPayload); assert findAuditEvent("hub.rebuild.fail").Metadata["reason"] != nil

tests.title: Worktree creation and removal are each logged at info level with the workspace slug and worktree path
given: a successful rebuild run for "acme"
then: an info log line for creation names "acme" and the worktree path
an info log line for removal names "acme" and the same path
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert logger.InfoCalls contains substring("acme") && substring(worktreePath); assert logger.InfoCalls contains a second entry with same slug/path for removal

tests.title: Per-rebuild and hub-startup stale-worktree cleanups each log every removal at info level with the workspace slug and path
given: a stale directory <root>/acme/rebuild/old-job exists at rebuild time, and another at hub startup
tests.when: the per-rebuild cleanup runs, then separately the startup cleanup runs
then: both log an info line naming "acme" and the removed path
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert logger.InfoCalls contains substring("acme/rebuild/old-job"); startupCleanup(root, ["acme"]); assert logger.InfoCalls contains substring("acme/rebuild")

tests.title: The one-time _rebuild_temp deletion is logged at info level with the workspace slug
given: _rebuild_temp exists in the trunk for "acme"
then: an info log line names "acme" and mentions the deletion
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctx, payload); assert logger.InfoCalls contains substring("acme") && substring("_rebuild_temp")

tests.title: Rebuild status responses, job records and audit event types are unchanged except for the addition of source_sha and hub.rebuild.followup
given: a completed rebuild with a stale patch tip triggering a follow-up
then: every field present before this change is still present with the same name and type
patch_results[] now also carries source_sha
the only new audit event type observed is hub.rebuild.followup
tests.pseudocode: rec := doRequest(GET,'/rebuilds/'+jobID); resp := decode(rec.Body); assert hasAllLegacyFields(resp); assert resp.PatchResults[0].SourceSHA != ""; assert newAuditTypes(before,after) == {"hub.rebuild.followup"}

tests.title: Sync, rollback and rerere forget return 409 workspace_busy only during a rebuild's fetch and final phases, and succeed outside them
given: a rebuild for "acme" progressing through fetch phase, then patch application, then final phase
tests.when: POST /sync is attempted during each of the three windows
then: it responds 409 workspace_busy during the fetch phase
it responds without 409 during patch application
it responds 409 workspace_busy during the final phase
tests.pseudocode: assert doRequest(POST,'/sync').Code==409; assert doRequest(POST,'/sync').Code!=409; assert doRequest(POST,'/sync').Code==409

tests.title: docs/api.md describes the narrowed workspace_busy window for sync, rollback and rerere forget, and the whole-rebuild window for archive/reclone
given: the repository's docs/api.md file
tests.when: the "Workspace Lock" section and workspace_busy error-type row are read
then: the text states sync, rollback and rerere forget are rejected only during a rebuild's fetch and final phases
the text states archive and reclone are rejected for the whole rebuild via the rebuild-active guard
tests.pseudocode: doc := readFile("docs/api.md"); assert contains(doc,"fetch") && contains(doc,"final") && contains(doc,"rebuild-active guard")

tests.title: docs/carry_patch_workflow.md's rebuild algorithm section describes the worktree-based flow and pre-rebuild integration-branch visibility
given: the repository's docs/carry_patch_workflow.md file
then: it no longer describes creating a _rebuild_temp branch or checking out the trunk

tests.title: A rebuild applies patches in its own worktree while a concurrent sync request completes unaffected, and the integration branch updates at the end
given: a running hub with a real carry_patch workspace "acme" carrying two active patches
job queue dispatches a rebuild job carrying job id "job-42"
tests.when: the rebuild reaches patch application and, concurrently, POST /workspaces/acme/sync is called before the final phase starts
then: the sync call returns 200 without waiting for the rebuild
upstream_head_sha is updated by the sync
the rebuild subsequently reacquires the lock, force-updates the "deploy" branch to its worktree's final HEAD SHA, releases the lock, and removes acme/rebuild/job-42

tests.title: A push to an active patch branch mid-rebuild produces a follow-up rebuild that applies the new commit
given: a running hub with workspace "acme" and active patch branch "feature/a" at SHA A
a rebuild job is dispatched and has snapshotted "feature/a" at A
tests.when: a new commit A2 is pushed to "feature/a" while the rebuild is still applying patches, and the rebuild subsequently finishes and releases its final-phase lock
then: the completed rebuild's patch_results record source_sha A for that patch, unaffected by the push
a hub.rebuild.followup audit event is emitted naming "feature/a"
a new rebuild job with SubmittedBy "system:stale-snapshot" is enqueued and, once dispatched, applies A2

tests.title: A crashed rebuild's leftover worktree is reclaimed at hub startup and at the next rebuild, with no operator action needed
given: workspace "acme" has a leftover acme/rebuild/job-7 directory and in-progress cherry-pick state left by a simulated crash
tests.when: the hub process starts up and runs its startup cleanup, and a subsequent rebuild job for "acme" is dispatched
then: acme/rebuild/job-7 no longer exists once startup cleanup completes
the new rebuild job creates a fresh worktree and completes successfully without any trunk reset

tests.title: Archive is rejected with workspace_busy while a rebuild runs and succeeds once the rebuild finishes and clears its guard
given: a running hub with workspace "acme"
a rebuild job for "acme" is dispatched and sets the rebuild-active guard
tests.when: POST /workspaces/acme/archive is called while the rebuild is applying patches, then retried after the rebuild completes
then: the first call returns 409 workspace_busy and the workspace directory still exists
the retried call succeeds and the workspace directory is deleted
